text:
sam: Heads-up — CUST-8421 reporting embedding vector width changed after they pinned a model. They pinned what they thought was a 1024-dim model but are getting 768-dim vectors in production. Customer impact: search relevance dropped, noisy regression.

maria: Can you paste a minimal request/response and any runtime logs?

sam: Sure — reproducer from their environment (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1024@locked-2025-09-01","input":"hello world"}'
```
Response (trimmed):
```json
{
  "model":"open-embed-1024@locked-2025-09-01",
  "usage":{"input_tokens":2},
  "embedding": [0.001, 0.003, /* ... */ ]  // length: 768
}
```
Runtime log snippet from their request (from our gateway):
```
2025-09-12T14:45:40Z INFO request_id=xx embed.dim=768 model_alias=open-embed-1024@locked-2025-09-01 runtime_variant=open-embed-768-quant routing=variant-fallback
```

alex: That log line stands out — looks like we routed to a smaller quantized variant. Did the pin map to an alias that allows variant substitution?

chris: Quick check: the pin API supports locking to either an alias or a specific model digest. If they used the alias form (e.g., `open-embed-1024@locked-2025-09-01`) and that alias was remapped to an equivalent with different dims for memory reasons, fallback could happen. I will check model-catalog and routing rules. :eyes:

support-bot: Variant substitution event recorded at 1752467740: alias=open-embed-1024@locked-2025-09-01 substituted_with=open-embed-768-quant reason=capacity_constrained node_pool=gpu-v2

maria: Do we have any safety check that validates embedding length against model metadata before returning to customer? If not, we should at least log and return a 500 to avoid silent data corruption.

eng-ml: I'm on it — looking at the runtime trace and model registry now. Initial hypothesis: autoscaler evicted the 1024-capable variant on that region and the routing policy allowed a compatible-but-different-arch fallback. The model registry shows two variants under that alias.

sam: Customer wants a short-term workaround. Proposed options: 1) re-pin to the explicit model digest (sha256:abcd...), 2) force model= open-embed-1024-exact in the request, or 3) rollback the alias remap. Which is fastest?

alex: Fastest is re-pin to digest or rollback alias. We should not change runtime routing mid-incident without confirmation.

chris: Action items: eng-ml to confirm why alias had both variants, infra to check why capacity caused fallback, support to give customer repro steps to pin to digest. I'll create infra runbook ticket if we find autoscaler flapping.

eng-ml: Confirmed — alias contained both variants; the quantized 768 variant was marked compatible for many workloads but not for pinned embedding-width-sensitive customers. I'll open model-registry PR to split alias_tiers so pinned aliases cannot include width-changing variants.

maria: Also adding a quick guard in the embeddings router: if model metadata.embedding_dim != response_length then emit an error and a metric. Low-effort hotfix to reduce silent regressions.

sam: Communicated workaround to customer (re-pin to digest + temporary rollback option). Customer accepted re-pin for now. Marking P1 and assigning owners: eng-ml (investigate alias rules), eng-platform (routing guard), support (customer comms).

alex: Good. Keep thread updated with root-cause and PR links. :thumbsup:

chris: Noted — I'll post the model-registry PR and infra incident link here once available.

sam: Thanks everyone — closing loop after PR and metric are live.
